text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Pager -> High token usage detected for customer 'Voyager Health' (dedicated-vpc / vpool-7). Token count spike ~4.1x baseline starting 2026-03-15T03:12:03Z. Automatic throttles and billing alerts fired. Paging on-call.

Maya P: I'm on it, grabbing logs + will triage. Linking the metrics dashboard -> https://console.redwood.io/metrics/voyager/vpool-7

Tom H: Noted. Any idea if this is model-side or upstream preprocessing? Could be double-tokenization.

Liam C: Quick snapshot from the gateway logs shows a lot of requests with pre-tokenized arrays in the body. Example: 
```
REQUEST_ID=abcd1234 USER=voyager_health MODEL=gpt-4x TIMESTAMP=2026-03-15T03:12:05Z
payload={"input":"Patient has a fever...","tokens":[101,205,333,...]} tokens_in=1024 tokens_out=512 total_tokens=1536
```
Looks like some clients are sending token arrays and we still run our tokenizer, causing duplication.

Eva S: I can push a hotfix to the VPC edge to detect a tokens[] field and skip tokenization for those requests. But need to coordinate with infra so we don't break other customers.

Maya P: For immediate mitigation we should throttle Voyager's per-tenant token budget, and add a temporary token-count cap so billing and limits don't explode. Also notify support to inform the customer we are investigating.

Tom H: Agreed. I'm going to apply a conservative per-tenant hard cap via admin API. Patch command: 
```
# admin action - set tenant cap
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/voyager/limits \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"max_total_tokens_per_min":400000, "temp_action":"throttle"}'
```
Do not roll back until we confirm tokenization normalization.

Incident Bot: Action queued by Tom H. Throttle applied at 03:18:12Z.

Billing Bot: Flagging Voyager Health invoices for review. Temporarily pause automatic billing spikes, add manual review queue.

Jordan R: Support notified Voyager contacts at 03:20Z: "We're investigating elevated token counts; we've applied temporary throttles to limit billing impact. Will update shortly."

Liam C: I'm going to deploy the edge detection rule as a canary on vpool-7 (10% traffic) — rule will skip model tokenizer if payload includes "tokens" array and has a matching model token signature. Patch: 
```
if request.body.tokens and request.headers['x-client-tokenized']=='1':
  skip_tokenize=true
else:
  tokenize()
```
Deploying now to canary.

Maya P: Canary shows immediate drop in token accounting for those requests (samples):
```
before: total_tokens=1536 | after (canary): total_tokens=512
sample_request_id=abcd1234
```
That confirms double-tokenization.

Tom H: Good. Next steps: 1) Expand canary to full vpool-7, 2) Ask Voyager to stop sending pre-tokenized payloads or set x-client-tokenized header, 3) Make the detection rule permanent for that tenant only so we don't affect others.

Eva S: Deploying tenant-scoped rule now (03:32Z). Also adding an event to block requests that claim pre-tokenized but mismatch model signature.

Maya P: Billing will need an action: we recommend a credit for excess tokens from the window 03:12-03:32 UTC while misconfiguration persisted. Billing Bot, confirm process?

Billing Bot: Put Voyager on billing-hold for the spike window and create a credit request ticket assigned to @Jordan R. We'll estimate manual credit after postmortem.

Jordan R: Accepted. I'll follow up with customer success and legal if needed.

Tom H: Root cause hypothesis: Voyager's ingestion pipeline switched to sending explicit token arrays (pre-tokenized BPE) but didn't set x-client-tokenized header. Our general tokenizer then tokenized again. We should have a validation that rejects/normalizes token arrays unless tenant explicitly opted-in.

Maya P: Agreed. Action items (short):
- [Maya P] Expand canary to full vpool-7 and monitor (in progress).
- [Tom H] Keep tenant throttle until normalization verified (done).
- [Eva S] Add permanent tenant-scoped detection + mismatch rejection rule (in progress).
- [Liam C] Add automated metric alert for token_in/token_payload mismatch ratio.
- [Jordan R] Coordinate billing credit and customer comms.

Liam C: Pushing the mismatch alert rule now. Threshold set: if >5% of requests include a tokens[] payload AND the token_in/token_payload_ratio > 1.8 for 5m -> page oncall.

Incident Bot: Canary expanded to 100% at 03:35:02Z; token counts back to baseline. Throttle remains until tomorrow 12:00Z for safety.

Maya P: Final update for channel: Mitigation applied, root cause confirmed as upstream pre-tokenization without header; we've implemented tenant-scoped normalization + mismatch detection, temporarily throttled to limit billing, and queued a billing credit review. No broader customer impact observed. Closing pager but leaving follow-ups in postmortem.

Tom H: Postmortem items: create an automated sanitizer for token arrays, add integration test for clients sending tokens[], and update onboarding docs for VPC customers about token header.

Incident Bot: Incident closed at 2026-03-15T04:00:00Z.

Jordan R: I'll draft the customer communication and the billing adjustment note. Thanks team. :handshake:

Maya P: Great job everyone. Filing for postmortem and tagging eng-runtime + billing.

Reaction highlights: :thumbsup: from Tom H, :eyes: from Eva S, :spiral_notepad: from Jordan R.
